constraints: Define the new stop-event kinds as ONE closed, named taxonomy on the orchestrator-events ledger: dangling-prerequisite, no-op-cycle, prepare-skip, source-truncation, zero-grader-drop. Use stable kebab-case spellings shared with the fw status reader (built in a dependent task). Mirror the existing five-member claim-event taxonomy's shape rather than inventing a parallel ledger.

Each record names its subject task/source and carries the cause in its payload: the missing prerequisite id; the no-op reason plus observed/target queue depth; the prepare failure text; the source name and the truncation/zero-grader detail.

Append-only and same-transaction where a committed state change exists (D-3): the prepare-skip record is written in the same store transaction as the claim release it accompanies; records that accompany no state change are still appended exactly once per occurrence. Provide NO update/delete for these rows.

Do NOT dedupe or coalesce recurring stops (D-3): a prepare-skip recurring every cycle, or a no-op cycle every pass, produces one record per occurrence -- the recurrence IS the signal. A ledger that collapses N occurrences into one must fail.

Audit-witness only (D-2): record the stop WITHOUT changing what gets scheduled. The dangling-prereq task stays out of the ready set; the prepare-skip still releases the claim and continues draining; the no-op cycle still emits zero tasks; the truncated/zero-grader work sequence returned to the caller is byte-for-byte unchanged (the record is a pure side channel).

Route the source truncation and zero-grader signals through the production _policy source builders (wire the log/sink to the durable record there), not only through a test-injected callable -- the gap today is that production passes nothing.
Commit the change with a clear message before reporting done.
non_goals: Do NOT add any retry, respawn, re-author, re-drive, or auto-skip-forever behavior -- visibility only.

Do NOT alter the work sequence a source returns, the ready-set membership of a dangling-prereq task, the autopilot emit count, the claim-release/continue control flow on prepare failure, or the page/item limits themselves.
Do NOT create a synthetic lifecycle or run_id for these pre-run stops (D-1) -- they have no run; they belong on the per-task orchestrator-events ledger, not the per-run domain-event stream.
Do NOT add pruning, retention, rotation, or a growth cap to the ledger; do NOT change the existing five claim-event kinds.
Do NOT weaken or delete any assertion under packages/flywheel-orchestrator/tests/.
Do NOT modify flywheel-core, the persistence-schema*.sql files, or the per-run domain-event stream here (separate task).
edge_cases: Items where A declares a prerequisite on a non-existent id: one orchestrate pass records a dangling-prerequisite row for A naming the missing id, and A stays out of the ready set -- recording the row but making A runnable, or making A runnable without a row, must both fail.

A source backing returning 201 items at a 200 page limit records exactly one source-truncation row naming the source AND returns the same work sequence it returns today; an item carrying zero graders records one zero-grader-drop row AND is still dropped from the sequence as today.
A prepare-preflight failure recurring across three cycles records three prepare-skip rows (not one); a deduping ledger must fail.
An autopilot pass that DOES emit a grader-bearing task records NO no-op-cycle row -- a record on a productive cycle must fail.
